NOTES TO CONDENSED CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS:

On July 26, 1996, the Company sold through an underwritten initial public offering, 1,963,975 shares of its Common Stock at $10.00 per share, including 73,068 shares of Common Stock as a result of the Underwriters exercise of their Over Allotment Option. Upon closing the Company's initial public offering all outstanding shares of its Series A, C and D Redeemable Convertible Preferred Stock were converted into 6,716,997 shares of Common Stock, after giving affect to the Company's 1 for 2.7059046 reverse stock split effected in July 1996. The December 31, 1996 Consolidated Balance Sheet and

Consolidated Statement of Cash Flow reflect the impact of the initial public offering, the conversion of the Redeemable Convertible Preferred stock and the repayment of $2.0 million in bank term notes and $3.7 million payment of BioTek Acquisition Notes that occurred during calendar 1996. All
shares and per share amounts have been retroactively adjusted to reflect the reverse stock split.
Net income (loss) per share is computed using the weighted average number of shares of common stock outstanding, except as noted below. Common equivalent shares from stock options

and warrants are excluded from the computation because their effect is antidilutive; except that, pursuant to the Securities and Exchange Commission Staff Accounting Bulletins and Staff Policy, common and preferred shares, options and warrants issued during the period commencing 12 months prior to the initial filing of the initial public offering at prices below the public offering price are presumed to have been exercised in contemplation of the public offering and have been included in the calculation as if they were outstanding for all periods presented, determined by using the treasury stock method and the price from the initial public offering.

The balance sheets from December 31, 1995 and 1996 have been derived from the audited financial statements at that date but do not include all of the information and footnotes required by generally accepted accounting principles for complete financial statements.
